skyline.about: The 360-degree sunset skyline behind the fight (src/fight/skyline.ts): a 10:1 strip (src/assets/skyline/, baked by scripts/skyline-bake.mjs with its two ends cross-faded over seamOverlapPx so the wrap has no seam) on a cylinder of `radius` m and `heightMetres` m that follows the camera, its horizon (`horizonFraction` down the strip) at the camera's eye level, unlit, unfogged, drawn first with no depth write; the sand floor, its colour, grid and fog are untouched and draw over it. The flat `sky` colour shows until the strip lands (fetched after the first frame, `loadAfterFirstFrameMs` later), then it fades in over `fadeSeconds`. `brightness` multiplies the strip (1 = as painted) so the hero and boss stay readable; `yawDegrees` turns the strip about the vertical. ?sky=v1 (`query` = `v1`) draws today's flat sky and fetches nothing. 8192 wide WebP q82: Dom's quality-first pick, see the PR's size table. YAW FOLLOW (Dom 2026-10-27: the alien was rarely seen): the strip turns by `yawDegrees` + `yawFollow` x the camera's yaw (0 = fixed in world yaw, 1 = glued to the view), eased over `yawFollowSeconds` so it drifts after a turn like a far backdrop; `followOffsetDegrees` -90 (the follow only) puts the alien dead ahead at the page's first heading (about 8 degrees). `face` is the alien face centre in the picture (fraction across, down; the test reads it to keep the face in the clear sky band above the HUD at 375 wide). ?skyfollow=v1 (`followQuery`, `followV1`) = fixed in world yaw at `yawDegrees` (0), as before.

plate.about: The skyline as a far backdrop PLATE (src/fight/skyplate.ts; Dom 2026-10-27, portrait phone: the 360-degree strip showed a tenth of a 10:1 picture blown up to a pink blur and the alien face could never fit). The plate is a `spanDegrees` arc of the strip's far cylinder (`radius`), facing the camp (it follows the camera's heading with the strip's follow rows, ?skyfollow=v1 pins it there): the face is dead ahead of the page's first heading (about -Z), turned by `turnDegrees` more (derived from `face`, so a new picture needs no yaw row), showing the picture `file` (src/assets/skyline/) at its NATIVE aspect, never stretched: a window of the picture `cropAspect` wide to tall is cut around `face` (u, v: the alien face centre as a fraction across and down the picture; the whole picture when it is no wider than that), and the arc is as tall as that window needs at its width. `horizonFraction` is the picture's horizon row, a fraction down it. `faceElevationDegrees` puts the face that many degrees above the eye's level (so the pitched-up phone camera has it in view; the picture's own horizon then sits below the eye, where the cloud sea meets the melted sand). The edges fade to nothing (`edgeFadeFraction` each side, `topFadeFraction`, `bottomFadeFraction`, fractions of the plate) into a plain sky gradient (`sky`: `hazeColor` at the bottom, `horizonColor` at the picture's horizon row, `topColor` at the top, a cylinder `halfHeightMetres` either side of the eye, `rings` rows) that is the sky everywhere else. DESIGNER LAYER SET (2026-10-27): `file` is now the designer's CLEAN plate 01_clean_plate.webp, 4096x1024 (4:1, recompressed to WebP q80, 251 KB -> 134 KB; no globe, no planet, registered to the first picture within 0 px so `face`, `horizonFraction` and `cropAspect` are unchanged); the planet and globe cut-outs go over it (anim.about, docs/SKY-LAYERS.md). `flatFile` (the first flattened 2508x627 picture, skyline-titan.webp) with `flatQuery`/`flatValue`: ?skyflat=1 shows it with none of the layers. THE FIRST PICTURE (Dom's Smiling Cosmic Titan Over Cloudsea, 2508x627 = exactly 4:1, shown whole at native proportions, WebP q88, 121 KB; horizon 80% down, face centre at 58.5% across and 63% down, moon and face in the middle half, edges fade to the sky colour, the top 40% plain blue): swapping the picture again is `file`, `cropAspect`, `horizonFraction` and `face`; nothing else changes (a picture wider than `cropAspect` is cut to that window around `face`, a narrower one is shown whole). The arc draws at SKYLINE_ORDER + `orderOffset`, over the folded cloud floor (fold.orderOffset) and under the sand, so inside its span the picture's own cloud sea shows and the floor's clouds carry on either side and below it; the plain sky gradient draws first of all. The old 360-degree strip's picture (`skyline.file`, 7782x820) stays for the rollback: ?skyplate=v1. ?skyplate=v1 (`query` = `v1`) draws the old whole 360-degree strip. ?sky=v1, ?skyfollow=v1 and ?skyfold=v1 keep their meaning.

anim.about: THE PLATE'S LAYERS AND SMALL CODED MOTION (src/fight/skyanim.ts; Dom 2026-10-27 'small motion on the static image'; the designer's registered layer set of the same day, 4096x1024, manifest.json). Presentation only: the plate material gets a few shader lines and uniforms, so a frame costs one clock tick and a few uniform writes (no texture re-upload, no extra draw). `plate.file` is the CLEAN plate (no globe, no planet); the planet and globe cut-outs are composited over it at their registered place, so they are part of the picture. Every layer file is named by its row (a .webp or .png in src/assets/skyline/): a re-delivery is a file swap. Positions are fractions across (u) and down (v, y down) the PLATE picture, radii are fractions of its WIDTH; a `rect` is the crop of the layer picture that is kept (u0,v0,u1,v1, fractions of the plate), so the GPU holds small textures, not full-size ones. `on`/`query`/`off`: ?skyanim=off stops the MOTION (the layers still composite: they are the picture); `respectReducedMotion` true = prefers-reduced-motion stops it too; the clock stops while the tab is hidden. `on` false draws no layers at all and is only right with a flattened plate (?skyflat=1 uses plate.flatFile, the old flattened picture, with none). `readyTimeoutSeconds`: the plate waits this long for the layer pictures so a layer never pops in. A layer with `on` false is not even fetched. PLANET: `file` = RGBA cut-out of the red planet (registered to the plate), `rect`, `centre`, `radius`; `glow` is a faint rim glow that pulses (`color`, `strength`, `pulseSeconds`, `lowerFadeFrom` = disc-radius y below which the glow fades out, where the cloud sea crosses the disc; `on` false = static planet). GLOBE: `file` = RGBA cut-out, `rect`, `centre`, `radius`; `spin` = a fake spin of the cut-out's own pixels (longitude shifted and mirror-folded so it never seams; `secondsPerTurn`, `swingDegrees` 0 = a continuous turn, above 0 = a swing of that many degrees each way); `highlight` = a soft moving glint (`strength`, `size` and `orbit` in disc radii, `lift`, `orbitSeconds`); `sprite` = the designer's 24-frame turn sheet (`file`, `columns`, `rows`, `frames`, `frameSeconds` per frame step, `cellPx` = a frame cell in the sheet, `ballRadiusPx` = the sphere's radius inside a cell, `sheetPx`, `loadScale` = the sheet is downscaled by this when it lands, `rects` = each frame's x,y,w,h in the sheet); sprite.on false by default because its frames read as a pink arch on a blue ball, not a clean world. GLISTEN: `file` = the designer's greyscale mask (white = may shimmer; the halo structure stays still), `rect` = the crop kept, `spreadTexels` = the speckles are a pixel or two so they are grown this many texels, `color`, `strength`, `baseGlow` = the always-on part of the shimmer, a sweep band `width` wide, tilted by `slant`, crossing the rect in `sweepSeconds` every `periodSeconds` adds to it, and `twinkle` (`periodSeconds`, `cells` across the plate, `amount` 0..1) shifts the highlights. SWAPPING: new plate = plate.file (same 4:1 shape; change cropAspect/face/horizonFraction only if the shape or face moves); new layer = its `file` (and rect/centre/radius if it moves); docs/SKY-LAYERS.md lists the files. SKY LIFE (Dom 2026-10-27 'more life on the smiling titan'; no new art, every number a row, each effect its own `on`, all stopped by ?skyanim=off, reduced motion and a hidden tab): SPARKLE = a procedural 4-point star glint drawn in the shader (no texture): every `minGapSeconds`..`maxGapSeconds` (seeded by `seed`, never twice on the same anchor in a row, the first after `firstDelaySeconds`) one of `anchors` (u, v = a point of the plate picture as fractions across and down, on the grin's teeth and the crown jewels; `scale` multiplies `size`) flashes for `durationSeconds` (fast rise, slow fall) with arms `size` (a fraction of the plate's WIDTH), `strength` and `color`; it rides with the breathing body. CROWN GLOW = a soft slow pulse of additive light over the crown's ring-tech (`centre`, `radiusU` across and `radiusV` down, fractions of the plate width; `color`, `strength` 0..1, `pulseSeconds`). BREATHING = the body and belly rise and fall: the picture is sampled `amplitudePx` plate pixels up and down (a sine of `periodSeconds`, `phase` 0..1 of a turn) inside `rect` (plate fractions) and the lift fades to nothing over `featherFraction` of the rect's size at every edge, so the clouds, the horizon, the rings and the outer arms stay still and the face and crown move as one with the body; the glisten mask and the sparkles follow the lift. GLOBE BOB: `globe.bob` floats the globe cut-out (and its glint) `amplitudePx` plate pixels up and down over `periodSeconds` from `phase`. PACK 2 (the designer's second pack, docs/SKY-LAYERS-manifest-2.json; every file named by a row): `plate.file` is now 13_plate_fixed.webp (ghost smudge and horizon blur fixed, same registration). EYES: the RGBA patches `blink.file` (both closed) and `wink.file` (viewer-left closed) at `rectPx` (x, y, w, h in plate pixels, drawn native, straight alpha, riding with the breathing body); a seeded event every `intervalMinSeconds`..`intervalMaxSeconds` after `firstDelaySeconds`, held `holdMinSeconds`..`holdMaxSeconds` (blink 0.09-0.14, wink 0.15-0.24), cross-faded over `fadeSeconds`, a wink about every `wink.everyEvents` events (+/- `everyJitter`, never two winks in a row), the patch edge feathered `featherPx` plate pixels so no seam or hairline shows (the patches ship with non-zero alpha on their edges). DROOL: `shimmer` = the full-plate greyscale mask cropped to `rectPx`, a slow additive light (`color`, `strength`, `periodSeconds`, `waves` along the streak, `spreadTexels`) travels down the stationary streak; `drop` = a droplet spawned at `spawnPx` (anchor `anchorPx` inside its sprite) every `spawnMinSeconds`..`spawnMaxSeconds` (seeded, first after `firstDelaySeconds`), falling `fallDistancePx` plate pixels from `startSpeedPx` per second with `accelPx` per second squared, fading in over `fadeInSeconds` and out over the last `fadeOutPx`, at `strength`; the plain sprite `file` below `stretchFromSpeedPx` per second, `stretchedFile` at and above it. PLANET `sphere`: a real turning world: `file` (equirectangular, wraps across, clamps up and down, downscaled by `loadScale`) mapped on a sphere inside the planet disc (`centre`, `radius`) and turned once per `secondsPerTurn` (starting `startTurns` of a turn round), the designer's `shading` overlay fixed on top (scaled so its disc, `discFraction` of the picture, matches the planet's radius, alpha-blended at `strength`); the cut-out's own alpha still decides what shows, so the cloud horizon keeps hiding the planet's lower part; `sphere.on` false = the old flat cut-out (rollback).

views.about: How much of the strip shows (src/fight/skyview.ts). Dom picked B (2026-10-27): `default` names the variant the page draws with no link; ?skyview=a|b|c picks one; ?skyview=v1 (`v1`) is the look before this (no melt, no lowering, nothing here runs); ?sky=v1 is still the flat sky. The camera, zoom and fight framing are never touched. Per variant: fogColor ('' = the scene's) is the strip's horizon haze (its lower band at horizonFraction, as drawn at `brightness`) and fogDensity (0 = the scene's, exp-squared) fogs the far sand into it; fadeStartDegrees / fadeEndDegrees (0/0 = off) melt the sand and its grid to transparent by how far below the horizon the camera sees it (solid at start and steeper, gone at end and shallower; an angle so it follows the strip's lowered bottom edge at any camera height, the phone fight camera looks 32 degrees down so its top edge is 8.6 degrees under the horizon), so the strip behind shows; dropMetres lowers the whole strip (the horizon of the image sits that far below the eye), heightMetres (0 = the row's) resizes it; brightness replaces the strip's own so the HUD reads over its bright cloud band. foeFade (true/false) fades the opponents and their gear by the same band measured at their feet, so a far boss dissolves into the clouds where the sand under him does (src/fight/foefade.ts; the hero is never faded; needs a band); ?foefade=v1 (foeFadeQuery / foeFadeV1) turns it off. A = fog only; B = fade + lowered strip + haze fog; C = lowered strip only.

fold.about: The folded floor (src/fight/skyfold.ts, Dom 2026-10-27: fold the image so the lower part becomes the floor). The strip's lower cloud band is laid flat on the ground under the sand: its horizon row (variant bandTopFraction, a fraction of the image height down from the top) is the far edge at farMetres, its bottom edge (bandBottomFraction) the near edge at nearMetres, the picture's x following the cylinder's yaw so the clouds under the horizon line up with the sky above. Rows are spaced the way a flat floor is seen (equal steps in 1/distance), so the clouds shrink toward the horizon. It follows the camera, sits at groundY, is unlit and unfogged, draws at SKYLINE_ORDER + orderOffset (after the strip, before the sand) with no depth write, and fades in with the strip; the far featherFraction of it fades to nothing so it melts into the sky behind. Only built when the sand melts (?skyview is not v1) and the strip is on. ?skyfold=v1 (`v1`) builds nothing; ?skyfold=a|b picks a variant, `default` is the no-link one (B: A's rows pulled across the ground are streaky spikes, B is the same band softened). A reuses the strip's own texture (file empty, no download); B loads `file` (src/assets/skyline/, baked by scripts/skyfold-bake.mjs: the band softened and tileable) after the first frame. around / rings are the mesh's segment counts.

duel.about: The arena theme V1's scene (src/fight/scene.ts) lights the duel with, in place of an arena-themes.json row: V2's sky, hemisphere and sun, the sun pushed out along V2's direction to clear V1's shadow frustum (near 1, far 70). V1's own exposure-dependent effects read `exposure`; `floor` names the arena-defs.json floor row the foot dust uses.
